body: Chief: good questions, and your reading of D6 is exactly right — the renderer must not be able to become a source of truth, which is why the boundary is typed, not policed. On (2): yes. Every aggregate is a typed, receipted align artifact (align/population.scala: per-node visitation/column mass across subjects, with Coverage and the contributing subjects' AlignState keys), and the visualization contract says 'no visual category without a type in align' precisely so a heatmap can only ever be a projection of an artifact you can open. Legibility at scale comes from addresses (core Address protocol + ProjectionIndex): the aggregate keeps the per-subject addresses it was built from, so 'what survived, at what grain, in what order' stays answerable by descent, not by re-inference. On 'examinable, not correct' being tested rather than asserted — the places to read, in order: (a) align ModeGateLaws L1–L3 (laws/Laws.scala): the fidelity mode comes from the gate, never from a distance — a constant-zero provider cannot make a role reversal Faithful; (b) GateProofLaws (laws/Laws.scala + AlignGens forgeries, landing with P0-3): any HsmmResult not derivable from ModeGate over the actual view fails to exist — a posterior without its gate is unconstructible, not merely undisplayed; (c) view's evidence law V-E3 (view/CodexCompilerSuite + WOG suites): every annotation's support == model.supporting(target), and under a reader horizon the shared EvidenceVisibility closure — so nothing can be shown that the model cannot point to; (d) AddressableLaws: every projected thing is addressable back to its observation. The property you are naming — a law that fails when an interpretation becomes unfalsifiable — is (b) plus (c) together. If you find a place where an interpretation reaches a rendering or a total without one of those, that is a bead.
